note: WP-00 proposed ledger. Each entry records an intentional ltmrs deviation from pinned Lemma 0.21.0 behavior. A consumer needing exact upstream behavior uses a reference profile or upstream; these are not silent.

deviations.upstream_behavior: TF-IDF lexical ranking only; scores are raw TF-IDF/RRF values.
deviations.ltmrs_behavior: Dense Candle embeddings + hybrid lexical/dense RRF + graph-aware context + normalized native scoring (held-out calibration open, AD-05).
deviations.user_visible_impact: Different result ordering and score interpretation; no byte-identical equivalence.
deviations.release_wording: Complete supported Lemma API/workflow surface with documented retrieval enhancements.

deviations.upstream_behavior: confirm=true stores a fragment verbatim despite secret detection.
deviations.ltmrs_behavior: confirm=true stores non-critical secrets verbatim; critical secrets (PEM private-key blocks, GitHub PATs, AWS AKIA keys) are always auto-redacted even with confirm=true.
deviations.reason: Security hardening must be named, never silent redaction (Part I 12.1).
deviations.user_visible_impact: confirm=true no longer bypasses redaction for critical irrevocable credentials; the response notes the critical override.
deviations.release_wording: Secret detection is best-effort with extended coverage; critical irrevocable credentials are never stored verbatim, confirm=true only overrides non-critical secrets.

deviations.ltmrs_behavior: Sessions bound to authenticated frontend channels; no daemon-global current session.
deviations.reason: RV-05: multi-agent correctness requires per-channel session isolation.
deviations.user_visible_impact: Concurrent independent frontends stay isolated; legacy single-client behavior preserved per channel.
deviations.release_wording: Session isolation across concurrent frontends; per-channel legacy semantics retained.

deviations.upstream_behavior: source is a free-form string stored verbatim; the detail icon is 'ai' -> robot, anything else -> person.
deviations.ltmrs_behavior: source is a strict enum (user|ai|web|paper|book|code) with disjoint documented rules; truly-unknown values coerce to ai at add time (verification state stays out — see feedback counts).
deviations.reason: Strict domain typing (AGENTS.md); the real upstream DB contains non-canonical source values (e.g. 'user-corrected formal review') that the enum cannot express.
deviations.user_visible_impact: Corpus values render and count correctly (non-ai shows the person icon, matching the upstream rule). Truly-unknown strings still render the robot icon and count under ai, where upstream would show the person icon and the original string.
deviations.test: T-MCP-02 (differential detail/summary wire tests); provenance_vocabulary_round_trips, memory_stats_groups_expanded_provenance
deviations.release_wording: Source is normalized to the canonical provenance vocabulary (user|ai|web|paper|book|code); values outside it coerce to ai.

deviations.upstream_behavior: Ranks context injection and empty-query recall with injectionScore (confidence*0.7 + recency*0.3); computes a composite quality_score on every fragment touch.
deviations.ltmrs_behavior: Uses its own normalized native scorer (held-out calibration open, AD-05) (design 10.3) for ranking; quality_score is an optional passthrough field, never computed natively.
deviations.reason: Intentional retrieval enhancement (Part I 10.3); upstream formulas retained as reference oracles (reference::injection_score, reference::calculate_quality_score) for differential testing only.
deviations.user_visible_impact: Different recall/injection ordering and no live quality_score values; neither formula is exposed on the wire.
deviations.test: T-RANK-01, T-RANK-02; differential tests calculate_quality_score_matches_upstream, injection_score_matches_upstream
deviations.release_wording: Enhanced native ranking; upstream quality/injection formulas preserved as frozen reference oracles, not native behavior.

deviations.upstream_behavior: Project attribution auto-detected from client working directory.
deviations.ltmrs_behavior: Stable project identity preferred (prj_<name>_<ulid>, ULID = 48-bit ms time + 80-bit CSPRNG); bound via `<checkout>/.ltmrs/project.json` (0600, `ltmrs project bind`) or the LTMRS_PROJECT_ID env override. Cwd is a fallback clue only (provisional legacy scope, never silent attribution). Shadow ambiguity refuses with candidates plus the `project bind` remediation; explicit id/all reads proceed with a warning. Sessions and writes carry the stable project_id (dual-written with the legacy bare string for display/export). Explicit `ltmrs project adopt --slug` attaches a cross-name legacy bucket with a shared-visibility warning when the slug is already attached elsewhere.
deviations.reason: Part I 01:§6.3 mandates stable native identity distinct from directory basenames (never silently merge same-name checkouts); daemon-side cwd observation is unavailable and spoofable, so cwd stays a clue, not an identity (owner ruling).
deviations.user_visible_impact: Unqualified access in a project dir sees that dir's legacy bucket plus global (own knowledge, not other projects'); ambiguous names refuse with qualification guidance; bound checkouts scope recall to their identity plus attached legacy and global.
deviations.test: T-MCP-02; T-SCOPE-02 (same-basename isolation, id-resolution order env > bind > cwd, shadow-refusal matrix a-d, moved-checkout root update, legacy-attached visibility)
deviations.release_wording: Stable project identity with checkout binding; cwd is a fallback clue, never an identity.

deviations.upstream_behavior: Fuzzy duplicate refusal on near-identical adds (plus auto-link on add).
deviations.ltmrs_behavior: Duplicate detection via 0.80 word-overlap threshold; auto-link behavior differs (see workflow notes).
deviations.reason: Deterministic, testable duplicate policy independent of upstream heuristics.
deviations.user_visible_impact: Near-duplicate adds may be refused or linked differently than upstream.
deviations.release_wording: Duplicate handling follows documented ltmrs thresholds, not upstream heuristics.

deviations.upstream_behavior: Ships 4 seed fragments; appends coaching blocks to session output; auto-detects technologies; suggests distill on session end; read ordering differs.
deviations.ltmrs_behavior: No seed fragments; no coaching blocks; no technology auto-detection; no distill suggestion; canonical read ordering.
deviations.reason: Instructional content and catalog seeding are host/model concerns, not canonical store behavior.
deviations.user_visible_impact: Fresh stores start empty; session output contains no coaching text.
deviations.release_wording: No seeded content or coaching output; workflow activation is host-driven.

deviations.upstream_behavior: Per-host skill paths with verified host behavior.
deviations.ltmrs_behavior: Mechanism-based host recipes; entries are documented recipes, not verified per-host behavior.
deviations.reason: Host matrix verification requires tested host versions not yet exercised.
deviations.user_visible_impact: Install recipes may need adaptation per host version.
deviations.release_wording: Host support is recipe-based; per-host verification pending.

deviations.ltmrs_behavior: The production backend contains no SQLite engine (RQ-21 native-code policy on the minimal core build). Legacy .lemma-backup payloads import ONLY through the isolated runtime helper (crates/lemma-import cdylib, own excluded workspace, dlopen at runtime, never linked into the daemon). Direct/native-restore paths still refuse legacy payloads explicitly with reason + import pointer; native .ltmrs-backup is the supported interchange path.
deviations.reason: Opening SQLite requires a C database engine excluded from the minimal core build; the isolated runtime helper is the permitted exception (01:464, owner-ordered Wave B5c).
deviations.user_visible_impact: Legacy backups import via backup_import_lemma (loss-accounted preview + confirm); they are never converted silently and never touch the production build graph.
deviations.test: T-IMPORT-02; fixture round-trip + tool preview/execute tests (Wave B5c)
deviations.release_wording: Legacy Lemma backups import through an isolated runtime helper; native backup/restore unchanged.

deviations.upstream_behavior: hybrid flag Default: false (pure TF-IDF); absent means lexical-only.
deviations.ltmrs_behavior: hybrid is Option<bool>: absent/true runs the enhanced hybrid engine when a dense backend is attached (current default); Some(false) serves the Lemma-faithful TF-IDF reference profile — corpus-wide TF-IDF cosine over the served snapshot with the upstream tokenizer/stopwords, augmented TF, smoothed IDF, 0.15 threshold, score-descending order and abstention on empty ranking (reference port of upstream semantic.ts) — with no dense leg and no FTS index.
deviations.reason: Dense backend is the calibrated default path; explicit opt-out restores parity (Part I 11.2). The reference profile is a behavior port of the upstream default path, verified by hand-computed toy-corpus tests plus a hybrid:false end-to-end behavioral pin.
deviations.user_visible_impact: Absent hybrid returns dense-enriched results where upstream returns TF-IDF-only; pass hybrid:false for upstream TF-IDF behavior (same tokenizer, 0.15 threshold and abstention semantics; tie order is EntityId-ascending as the declared divergent substitute for upstream row order).
deviations.test: hybrid absent/explicit unit tests in frontend::mcp (I8); retrieval::tfidf toy-corpus ranking/order/threshold/abstention tests; semantic_search_hybrid_false_uses_tfidf_profile + semantic_search_hybrid_false_skips_dense_leg (daemon tools)
deviations.release_wording: semantic_search runs hybrid retrieval by default; hybrid:false serves the upstream TF-IDF reference behavior.

deviations.upstream_behavior: Returns recall_explanation when explain:true (same applies_to/scope/notice/correction_tools/items shape as memory_read).
deviations.ltmrs_behavior: explain:true emits the ltmrs-native explanation object (engine readiness / dense-fallback mode, scope filter, partial flags) AND the upstream-shaped recall_explanation supplement (selection method tfidf_cosine/hybrid_rrf_mmr/fts5_bm25/substring_fallback per serving leg, with effective rank and score); default responses unchanged.
deviations.reason: Readiness/partial transparency required by design 10.x; additive fields, no wire regression. The native object is supplemented, never silently replaced (standing Wave B enrichment rule).
deviations.user_visible_impact: Both explanation objects only when explain:true is passed; default responses unchanged.
deviations.test: explain readiness unit tests in frontend::mcp (I8); semantic_search_hybrid_false/fallback/engine_explain_adds_recall_explanation (daemon tools)
deviations.release_wording: semantic_search accepts explain:true for a native readiness/partial explanation plus the upstream-shaped recall explanation.

deviations.upstream_behavior: Frozen schemas document max 100 (limit) and max 30 (topK); no baseline artifact records upstream handler semantics for out-of-range values.
deviations.ltmrs_behavior: Out-of-range limit/top_k (zero, above the per-tool page max, or beyond the pagination window) are typed Validation errors, not silent clamps to the page max; absurd offsets are likewise rejected instead of panicking or wrapping.
deviations.reason: Silent clamps and wrapping arithmetic misreport the served window; Wave A3a pagination honesty requires explicit rejection with the existing Validation envelope.
deviations.user_visible_impact: Requests with limit/top_k outside 1..=max (or any offset/limit beyond the 1000-item window, e.g. u64::MAX) now fail with a typed validation error instead of being clamped to an undocumented page; in-range behavior is unchanged.
deviations.release_wording: Out-of-range memory_read/semantic_search pagination values are rejected as validation errors instead of silently clamped.

deviations.upstream_behavior: Rebuilds tools/list tool descriptions per request with injected memory context.
deviations.ltmrs_behavior: Serves static frozen tool schemas verbatim; memory context is served in RESPONSES (recall_explanation, structured provenance, conflict notices) instead of injected descriptions. First-initialize freshness comes from a best-effort ListMemories prefetch before serving (Wave B1), degrading to the lazy first-call fetch on failure.
deviations.reason: Deterministic tool definitions (frozen conformance); no per-list token bloat; no stale injected snapshots under projection lag; revision-freshness comes from canonical reads.
deviations.user_visible_impact: tools/list descriptions never carry memory content; agents recall context via memory_read/semantic_search responses. Best-effort prefetch puts the non-empty store in the first initialize; a failed prefetch degrades to the lazy first-call fetch.
deviations.release_wording: Tool definitions stay static and deterministic; memory context is served in tool responses, not injected into tool descriptions.

deviations.upstream_behavior: Automatic conflict detection on add penalizes losing claims (confidence decay on the losing side).
deviations.ltmrs_behavior: memory_add runs the same conflict detection (scope-gated target-anchored scan) but refuses conflicting adds pre-commit with a Validation error carrying the conflicting id+title entries plus resolution advice (memory_update the superseded fragment first, then re-add; memory_relate contradicts once both claims exist). No memory is committed, no receipt or relations are recorded, and confidence is unchanged. Detection errors still degrade with a visible notice and commit. There is no override flag: a conflicting add cannot be pushed through.
deviations.reason: Owner direction for Wave B3b (2026-10-26, overrides B3 advisory-commit): a conflicting add must be refused — no silent path. Silent confidence mutation on an add would make recall non-reproducible and is never a legitimate side effect of storing a fragment; the losing-claim heuristic is deferred for later ad-hoc investigation.
deviations.user_visible_impact: Conflicting adds fail with a Validation error naming the conflicts and the remediation; conflicting fragments cannot coexist as separate live memories. Detection failures still succeed with a notice.
deviations.release_wording: Conflicting memory_add calls are refused with the conflicting ids/titles and remediation advice; no automatic confidence changes or links.
